A16-7.label: Psychological Drama
A16-7.defn: A drama whose engine is one person's inner state of trauma, guilt or obsession, rendered from inside (Peppermint Candy, Affliction, Death in Venice, The Master). A drama of mourning goes to Grief Drama, one of madness and mental illness to Mental Illness Drama; where suspense drives it, see A3; where the crisis is existential rather than psychological, A16-8.
A16-7.axis: by the inner condition: trauma and abuse first, then guilt and atonement, and obsession last

new_leaves.label: Grief Drama
new_leaves.breadth: Dramas of mourning: the bereaved spouse, parent or friend living through a death
new_leaves.defn: A drama whose subject is grief itself — a widow, widower, parent or friend living through loss, often in the long aftermath of a death (Three Colors: Blue, Maborosi, Manchester by the Sea, Drive My Car). A family collectively bereaved goes to Family Drama; a grief that becomes breakdown, to Mental Illness Drama.

new_leaves.label: Mental Illness Drama
new_leaves.breadth: Dramas of madness, breakdown, psychosis and the asylum
new_leaves.defn: A drama of a mind coming apart — schizophrenia, psychosis, depression, dissociation, breakdown — or of life in the asylum and clinic (Through a Glass Darkly, The Cobweb, Clean, Shaven, Spider, Take Shelter). A psychological thriller goes to A3; a grief drama to Grief Drama.
new_leaves.aliases: madness film; asylum drama; mental illness in film
new_leaves.axis: by era: the studio-era psychiatric drama, the anti-psychiatry and modernist decades, then the contemporary independent character study

A16-4.label: Father–Child Drama
A16-4.defn: A drama centred on a father and his child — the father–son or father–daughter bond strained, broken or repaired, into the father's old age (The Return, Aftersun, Fences, On Golden Pond, Like Father, Like Son). A mother and child goes to Mother–Child Drama; a drama of the whole family to A16-3; Japanese shomingeki to A16-1.
A16-4.axis: by the child and the stage of life: fathers and sons, fathers and daughters, then ageing fathers (and parents) with their adult children

new_leaves.label: Mother–Child Drama
new_leaves.breadth: Dramas of a mother and her daughter or son
new_leaves.defn: A drama centred on a mother and her child — the mother–daughter or mother–son bond, from childhood to the mother's old age (Autumn Sonata, Terms of Endearment, Mommy, I Killed My Mother, Room). A father and child goes to Father–Child Drama; a drama of the whole family to A16-3.
new_leaves.axis: by the child and the stage of life: mothers and daughters, mothers and sons, then ageing mothers (and grandmothers) with their adult children

A20-7.label: Art Film
A20-7.defn: A narrative feature whose avant-garde form (tableau, recitation, fragmentation, dream logic, anti-illusion) is its defining element (A Page of Madness, Limit, The Color of Pomegranates, Russian Ark, Holy Motors). The political-modernist 'counter-cinema' of Duras, Straub–Huillet, Godard and Rainer goes to Counter-Cinema; films made by gallery artists or for installation to Artists' Film & Video Installation; duration-based art films to A1-39 Slow Cinema.
A20-7.axis: by era: the silent and interwar avant-garde feature, the poetic cinema of the 1960s–80s, then the later art-house avant-garde by period

new_leaves.label: Counter-Cinema
new_leaves.breadth: Political-modernist narrative features of the 1960s–80s that dismantle illusion: text, recitation, distanciation
new_leaves.defn: A narrative feature in the political-modernist tradition Peter Wollen named 'counter-cinema': estrangement over identification, text and recitation over drama, the soundtrack split from the image, the narrative opened to theory (India Song, From the Clouds to the Resistance, Riddles of the Sphinx, Film About a Woman Who..., Salomé). Its core is 1968–1990, with its auteurs' later work; dream and tableau art films without that programme stay in Art Film.
new_leaves.aliases: political modernism; cinéma de la modernité; Brechtian cinema
new_leaves.axis: by national tradition: France and Belgium; Italy, Iberia and Greece; the German-speaking and Central European wing; the Anglo-American feminist wing; the Third Cinema wing

new_leaves.label: Artists' Film & Video Installation
new_leaves.breadth: Narrative and quasi-narrative works by gallery artists, and moving-image installations
new_leaves.defn: A moving-image work made by a visual artist from the gallery world, shown as a feature, a cycle or a multi-screen installation (Cremaster 3, Rape, Manifesto, Inconsolable Memories, Primitive). Underground and experimental filmmakers outside the art world stay in Art Film or their own leaves.
new_leaves.aliases: artists' cinema; gallery film; moving-image installation
new_leaves.axis: by form and period: installations and exhibitions, then artists' features before and after 2010

A19-9.defn: A documentary that takes a side on a public issue or follows a political movement, campaign or politician (Roger & Me, Harlan County U.S.A., 13th, The Square). Environmental causes go to Environmental Documentary, films made inside 1957–1990 militant movements to Militant Cinema, LGBTQ liberation and rights to LGBTQ Documentary; exposés of hidden wrongdoing to A19-10.
A19-9.axis: by the cause: first-person polemic, labour, civil and human rights, women's movements, elections and politicians, then protest and uprisings

new_leaves.label: Environmental Documentary
new_leaves.breadth: Documentaries of ecological causes: pollution, climate, food and animals, land defence
new_leaves.defn: A documentary that argues an ecological cause — industrial pollution and nuclear risk, climate change, the food system and animal welfare, or a community's defence of its land and water (Minamata, An Inconvenient Truth, Food, Inc., The Cove, Virunga). A nature film without an argument goes to Nature Documentary.
new_leaves.axis: by the cause: pollution and disaster, climate and the planet, food and animals, then land, water and indigenous defence

new_leaves.label: Militant Cinema
new_leaves.breadth: Documentaries made inside a movement as its weapon, 1957–1990: collectives, Newsreel, Third Cinema
new_leaves.defn: A documentary made from inside a struggle by its participants or a film collective, as an instrument of the movement rather than a report on it, in the cycle from the late 1950s to 1990 (The Battle of Chile, Summer in Narita, Finally Got the News…, The Nightcleaners, Patu!). Later activist films stay in Political Documentary.
new_leaves.aliases: cinéma militant; Third Cinema; Newsreel; collective documentary
new_leaves.axis: by national movement: Japanese collectives, Latin American Third Cinema, European militant collectives, North American Newsreel and Black radical cinema, then Asia, Africa and Oceania
secs: North American Newsreel & Black Radical Cinema

new_leaves.label: LGBTQ Documentary
new_leaves.breadth: Documentaries of gay, lesbian and trans liberation, AIDS activism and LGBTQ rights
new_leaves.defn: A documentary about LGBTQ people as a political community — gay liberation and its histories, AIDS activism, trans lives and the global fight for LGBTQ rights (Word Is Out, The Times of Harvey Milk, How to Survive a Plague, Kokomo City). A portrait of one queer artist goes to Biographical Documentary.
new_leaves.aliases: queer documentary; gay and lesbian documentary
new_leaves.axis: by the cause: liberation and queer histories, AIDS activism, then trans lives and LGBTQ rights worldwide

moves: Mike Tyson biography, not a political cause
history of the 1980 Iran hostage rescue mission
observational film of children with cancer; no political cause

A16-3.defn: A drama whose engine is the family as a group rather than one parent–child pair or one sibling bond: the household, the family gathered for a holiday or funeral, the inheritance, the home after a death (Still Walking, Rachel Getting Married, Summer Hours, Ordinary People). Siblings go to Sibling Drama; foster, adoptive and chosen families to Found Family Film; one parent and child to A16-4; a couple to A16-5.
A16-3.axis: by the family occasion: the household, then the gathered family, the inheritance, and the bereaved home last

new_leaves.label: Sibling Drama
new_leaves.breadth: Dramas of sisters, brothers and brother–sister bonds
new_leaves.defn: A family drama centred on siblings — sisters, brothers, or a brother and sister — their rivalry, devotion or estrangement (Rocco and His Brothers, The Makioka Sisters, You Can Count on Me, Our Little Sister, Frère et soeur). A drama of the whole family goes to Family Drama.
new_leaves.axis: by the sibling bond: sisters, brothers, then brother and sister and mixed sibling groups

new_leaves.label: Found Family Film
new_leaves.breadth: Dramas of foster, adoptive and chosen families
new_leaves.defn: A family drama whose family is made rather than born: the foster home and the orphan taken in, adoption and the search for birth origins, the chosen family of strangers (The Kid with a Bike, Secrets & Lies, Shoplifters, The Quiet Girl, Return to Seoul).
new_leaves.aliases: chosen family; foster family drama; adoption drama
new_leaves.axis: by how the family is made: fostering and orphans, adoption and birth origins, then chosen families

A14-1.defn: An American-tradition musical film whose songs and dances arise inside the story and carry plot and character, written for the screen or adapted from the stage (Top Hat, Meet Me in St. Louis, West Side Story, La La Land). Integrated musicals of other national cinemas go to European & World Film Musical; numbers staged as performances to A14-4; an all-sung film to A14-5.
A14-1.axis: by origin and audience: Hollywood studio originals, Broadway adaptations, family musicals, teen musicals, later screen originals, and the Astaire–Rogers cycle

new_leaves.label: European & World Film Musical
new_leaves.breadth: Integrated film musicals of national cinemas outside Hollywood
new_leaves.defn: A book musical — songs and dances carrying the story — made in a national film industry outside Hollywood: René Clair's French musicals, German Tonfilm comedies, the Soviet musical comedies of Aleksandrov and Pyryev, the Egyptian and Lebanese musical, the films of Demy and Honoré (Le Million, Volga-Volga, The Young Girls of Rochefort, Love Songs). Operettas go to Operetta Film; Hindi masala films, rumberas and comedia ranchera to their own leaves.
